title: Topological properties and phase diagram of the triangular Hofstadter model with staggered flux
abstract: We study the topological properties and phase diagram of the triangular Hofstadter model with staggered flux in adjacent triangles in this work. This lattice can be used to describe the low energy physics of the twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD) in a certain range of the electric displacement field between the two layers. We show that the Hofstadter spectrum of this model is generally asymmetric except at specific staggered flux $3φ= π/2 \mod π$ due to an additional P symmetry at such $φ$. Breaking the translation symmetry by dimerization lifts the P symmetry and results in rich topological phases in the system. The dimerized model with different rational external magnetic flux $Φ_B = 2πp/q$ has phase diagram with the following common features. For even q, the dimerized model generally has three gapped regimes. The one with small dimerization has finite Chern number and the other two have zero Chern number. For odd q, the model is gapped with zero Chern number at any finite dimerization. For both q even and odd, the two regimes with zero Chern number can be further characterized by the inversion symmetry of the parametrized one-dimensional chains of the system at φ= 0 \mod π/3$, and one regime is topologically non-trivial and the other is trivial. Our results may be tested in twisted bilayer TMD with weak interaction or cold atom systems in optical lattice or photonic crystals achieved in recent experiments.
summary: This work theoretically analyzes the topological phases of a triangular Hofstadter model used to simulate twisted bilayer TMDs. By studying how staggered flux and dimerization break symmetries, the authors map out complex phase diagrams characterized by quantized Chern numbers. The findings provide testable predictions for both solid-state materials and controllable cold atom systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the topological properties and phase diagram of the triangular Hofstadter model incorporating staggered flux.
main_result: The system exhibits rich topological phases dependent on whether the magnetic flux parameter q is even or odd, with distinct Chern number characteristics in different gapped regimes.
method: The analysis involves mapping the Hamiltonian to momentum space and calculating topological invariants (like the Chern number) by analyzing the energy spectrum's dependence on external fluxes and dimerization strength.
model_or_system: The model is the triangular Hofstadter lattice with staggered flux, relevant for describing twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). The Hamiltonian incorporates both a uniform magnetic flux ($\Phi_B = 2\pi p/q$) and an additional staggered flux term.
key_observables: Chern number ($C$), Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$), longitudinal conductivity ($\sigma_{xx}$), and the energy spectrum $E(\mathbf{k})$.
important_parameters: Rational external magnetic flux $\Phi_B = 2\pi p/q$, staggered flux parameter $\phi$, and dimerization strength ($\delta J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a tight-binding description for the low energy physics, and specific symmetries (like P symmetry) are analyzed at certain flux values.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Hofstadter spectrum for various fluxes and depict the phase diagram behavior based on the rational flux ratio $p/q$ and dimerization strength.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the Hamiltonian, then analyzes the effect of staggered flux symmetry. It proceeds to study the dimerized model's phase diagram separately for even and odd values of q, concluding with implications for experimental realization in TMDs or cold atoms.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter topology, the connection to moiré superlattices and tunable parameters (like electric displacement field) makes it highly relevant for AMO physicists working on engineered quantum systems using optical lattices or photonic crystals.
